en: to chat idly; to chatter away

examples.ko: 친구들과 카페에서 노닥거리다 보니 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: I chatted idly with friends at a cafe and time flew by.

examples.ko: 일은 안 하고 노닥거리지 말고 빨리 끝내세요.
examples.en: Stop fooling around chatting and finish up quickly.
My coworkers are chatting away in the break room.
We idled around gossiping during the lunch break.
I got scolded by the teacher for chatting during class.
Do your homework first instead of wasting time chatting.

explain: 별 의미 없는 이야기를 늘어놓는다는 뜻에 '할 일은 안 하고'라는 못마땅한 느낌이 함께 있어서 꾸짖을 때 자주 어울려요. 그냥 편하게 이야기하는 '수다 떨다'보다 더 부정적이에요.

phrases.example: 저 사람들은 일은 안 하고 계속 노닥거리고 있어요.
phrases.en: Those people are chatting away instead of working.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하고 있는 모습을 못마땅하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to disapprovingly describe what someone is doing right now.

phrases.en: Please don't chat idly during the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 꾸짖거나 부탁할 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative command form for scolding or asking someone to stop.

phrases.en: I spent time chatting idly at a cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)며'로 다른 행동과 이어 시간을 허비하는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linking with -(으)며 adds a sense of passing time idly.

explain_en: It means chatting about nothing in particular, with a disapproving feeling of 'instead of doing what you should', so it often fits a scolding. It is more negative than '수다 떨다', which is just casual chatting.

t90.ax: My coworkers are chatting away in the break room.

examples.ko: 식사 후에 차를 마시며 담소를 나눴어요.
examples.en: After the meal, we had a pleasant chat over tea.

examples.ko: 즐거운 담소 덕분에 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the pleasant chat, I didn't notice time passing.
I had some chat time with my friends for the first time in a while.
The family's cheerful chatter never stopped in the living room.
It was a relaxed get-together to chat, so there was no pressure.

examples.ko: 담소 분위기가 좋아서 저녁 모임이 길어졌어요.
examples.en: The chatting mood was so good that the evening gathering ran long.

explain: 웃으며 즐겁게 나누는 이야기를 말하고, '수다'보다 점잖고 격식 있는 느낌이에요. '담소를 나누다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요.

phrases.en: I chatted pleasantly with friends at a café.
phrases.nuance_ko: '담소'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말로, 즐겁게 이야기한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 담소, meaning to have a pleasant talk.

phrases.example: 점심 후에 짧은 담소 시간을 가졌어요.
phrases.en: We had a short chatting time after lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편하게 이야기하려고 따로 가진 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to time set aside for relaxed conversation.

phrases.en: The friendly chat continued even after dinner was over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 즐거운 이야기가 계속될 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a pleasant conversation keeps going.

explain_en: Pleasant relaxed conversation among people, often over tea. It means a cheerful, friendly conversation and feels more refined and formal than '수다'. The most common pairing is '담소를 나누다'.

examples.en: The players walk in, lined up in ranks.
The students formed a line on the playground.

examples.ko: 앞 대열에 서 있는 사람이 우리 선생님이에요.
examples.en: The person standing in the front line is our teacher.

examples.ko: 마라톤 대열 맨 뒤에서 천천히 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I ran slowly at the very back of the marathon pack.
My friend suddenly slipped out of the line.

examples.ko: 비가 와도 응원 대열은 흩어지지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even in the rain, the cheering crowd did not scatter.

explain: '줄'은 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '대열'은 행진이나 행사, 큰 무리처럼 질서 있게 늘어선 사람들에게 써요. '선진국 대열'처럼 어떤 집단이나 수준을 비유할 때도 나와요.

phrases.example: 저도 오늘부터 취업 준비생 대열에 합류했어요.
phrases.en: join the ranks of
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 무리나 흐름에 새로 들어가 함께하게 될 때 써요. 실제 줄이 아니라 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you newly become part of a group or trend. It is figurative, not about a real line.

explain_en: Organized rows of people moving or standing together — marching, groups. '줄' is the everyday word for a line. '대열' is used for orderly groups such as marches, events, or large crowds. It also works figuratively, as in '선진국 대열' (the ranks of advanced countries).

gh: one single straight row, one behind another

p.n: 일렬 cannot take 맞추다 this way; it only describes people forming a single row.

t90.ax: The players walk in, lined up in ranks.

examples.ko: 추석에는 성묘객 때문에 고속도로가 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: On Chuseok the highways get very congested because of people visiting graves.
Many people visiting graves gathered in front of the tomb.

examples.ko: 성묘객을 위해 임시 버스를 운영한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say they will run extra buses for people visiting graves.
It rained this year, so there were few grave visitors.

examples.ko: 묘지 주변에서 성묘객들이 음식을 차리고 있어요.
examples.en: Around the cemetery, grave visitors are setting out food.

examples.ko: 공원묘지 입구에 성묘객 차량이 길게 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: Cars of grave visitors lined up long at the entrance to the memorial park.

explain: '-객'은 관광객, 등산객처럼 어떤 일을 하러 온 사람을 가리켜요. 성묘객은 설이나 추석 즈음 뉴스에서 교통 소식과 함께 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '성묘하러 가는 사람들'처럼 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 성묘하러 가는 사람들 때문에 길이 막혀요.
phrases.en: The road is jammed because of the people going to visit graves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '성묘객'을 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spoken-style way of unpacking 성묘객 into plain words.

phrases.en: Grave visitors crowded the cemetery park during the Chuseok holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 명절 교통과 함께 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in holiday traffic news.

phrases.en: There is a bus running for grave visitors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '을/를'과 함께 써서 성묘객을 대상으로 한 서비스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the object particle, it describes a service aimed at grave visitors.

explain_en: The suffix '-객' marks people who have come to do something, as in 관광객 and 등산객. '성묘객' often appears in traffic news around Seollal and Chuseok. In casual talk people may say '성묘하러 가는 사람들' instead.

examples.en: A search party is looking for the missing hiker.
The search party combed the mountain all night.
They put together a search party of firefighters and soldiers.

examples.ko: 수색대에 지원한 사람이 백 명이 넘어요.
examples.en: More than a hundred people volunteered for the search party.
The rescue dogs also moved together with the search party.
Thanks to the search party's efforts, we found the child.

explain: 실종이나 조난 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. '구조대'는 사람을 구하는 팀이고, '수색대'는 먼저 찾아다니는 팀이라는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: The police sent a search party to the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾는 팀을 출발시킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when dispatching a search team.

phrases.en: The search party was dispatched right after the report.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in the news.

phrases.en: The search party members checked the paths all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수색대에 속한 한 사람 한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to individual members of the party.

explain_en: It often appears in news about missing or stranded people. A '구조대' is a team that rescues people, while a '수색대' is the team that goes out to find them first.

en: to buzz with a crowd; to teem noisily

examples.en: The market is swarming with people.
The classroom was so noisy that it was hard to start the lesson.
I can't stand places where bugs are swarming.
During breaks, the hallway is buzzing with kids.
Reporters were crowding noisily in front of the venue.
It was vacation time, so the amusement park was teeming with people.

explain: 사람이나 벌레가 한곳에 많이 모여서 시끄럽게 움직일 때 써요. '붐비다'는 소리가 없어도 쓰지만, 이 말은 시끌시끌한 느낌이 있어요. '와글와글'과 같은 계열의 말이에요.

phrases.en: Students are swarming noisily in the hallway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 다른 말로, 대화에서 '와글거리다'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A variant with the same meaning that can replace 와글거리다 in conversation.

phrases.en: I found my friend among the noisy crowd.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 형태로, 시끄럽게 모인 사람들을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, referring to people gathered noisily.

phrases.en: On the festival day, people swarmed the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 말하는 해요체로, 많은 사람이 모여 시끌시끌했던 장면에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past polite form, for a scene where many people gathered noisily.

explain_en: It is used when many people or bugs gather in one place and move around noisily. '붐비다' can be used even without noise, but this word carries a buzzing, noisy feel. It belongs to the same family as '와글와글'.

t90.ax: The market is swarming with people.

en: to buzz with voices; to murmur noisily; to be abuzz

examples.en: People are murmuring in the street over there.
When the accident happened, onlookers started buzzing.
I can hear a murmuring sound outside the classroom.
As the lecture was delayed, the students began to murmur.

examples.ko: 복도가 너무 웅성거려서 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The hallway is so noisy that I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 무대에 불이 꺼지자 관객들이 웅성거리다가 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: When the stage lights went out, the audience buzzed and then went quiet.

explain: 여러 사람이 낮은 소리로 두런두런 떠들 때 써요. '시끄럽다'와 달리 말소리가 뒤섞여 들리는 느낌이고, 부사 '웅성웅성'으로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: People are gathered, murmuring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 부사로 써서 소리가 뒤섞이는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, showing blended low voices.

phrases.en: People began to murmur.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웅성거리다'를 줄여 말하는 형태로 뜻이 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form with nearly the same meaning as 웅성거리다.

phrases.en: I can hear a murmuring sound outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 소리를 꾸며 주는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 turns it into a modifier for 소리 (sound).

explain_en: Use it when many people talk together in low voices. Unlike '시끄럽다' (loud), it suggests overlapping voices blending into a murmur, and the adverb '웅성웅성' is also common.

t90.ax: People are murmuring in the street over there.

en: meeting and parting; being together and splitting

examples.en: During election season, parties keep splitting and merging.

examples.ko: 이합집산이 잦은 모임은 신뢰를 얻기 어려워요.
examples.en: A group whose members keep coming and going struggles to earn trust.

examples.ko: 이 업계는 회사들의 이합집산이 아주 빨라요.
examples.en: In this industry, companies merge and split very quickly.

examples.ko: 정치권의 이합집산을 보면서 실망한 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people were disappointed watching the political world's shifting alliances.
After much splitting and regrouping, a new party was formed.

examples.ko: 친구 무리의 이합집산은 학교에서 흔한 일이에요.
examples.en: Friend groups forming and breaking up is common at school.

explain: 헤어지고 모이기를 되풀이한다는 뜻으로, 정당이나 단체가 이익에 따라 움직일 때 많이 써서 다소 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스나 신문 기사에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 작은 정당들이 이합집산해서 큰 당이 됐어요.
phrases.en: Small parties came together and split, and became a big party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 뒤에 '하다'를 붙인 동사로, 단체가 모이고 흩어지는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb form with 하다, describing groups gathering and splitting.
phrases.en_equiv: to come together and split apart

phrases.en: They keep forming and breaking alliances at every election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 일이 계속 되풀이된다는 뜻을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes that the same thing keeps repeating.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep forming and breaking up

phrases.en: Political groups are splitting and regrouping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 모임이 갈라지고 합쳐지는 상황을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news to report groups splitting and merging.

explain_en: It describes repeatedly breaking apart and regrouping, and is used for parties or organizations that shift according to their interests, so it can sound a bit negative. You'll often see it in news articles.

en: to be harmonious; to be amicable; to be friendly

examples.ko: 어제 가족 모임 분위기가 정말 화기애애했어요.
examples.en: The mood at yesterday's family gathering was really warm and friendly.
The meeting ended in a harmonious atmosphere.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 늘 화기애애해서 출근이 즐거워요.
examples.en: Our team is always so friendly that going to work is fun.
The cheerful mood suddenly went quiet.
Even though we had just met, we chatted in a warm, friendly way.

examples.ko: 회식 자리가 화기애애하지 않아서 일찍 나왔어요.
examples.en: The team dinner wasn't a friendly atmosphere, so I left early.

explain: 여러 사람이 모인 자리나 분위기가 따뜻하고 즐거울 때 써요. 사람 한 명에게는 쓰지 않아요. '훈훈하다'는 정이 느껴질 때, '화기애애하다'는 모두 사이좋게 웃고 이야기하는 분위기에 어울려요.

phrases.en: I chatted with my friends in a warm, friendly mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 써서 대화하는 모습이 다정하고 즐겁다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In adverb form, it says the conversation was warm and pleasant.
phrases.en_equiv: to talk in a friendly mood

phrases.en: Once the food came out, the gathering became lively and warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음에는 어색했던 자리가 점점 따뜻하고 즐거워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an awkward gathering gradually turns warm and pleasant.

phrases.en: The mood at the gathering was really heartwarming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화기애애하다보다 정이 느껴지는 따뜻함에 더 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the warmth of kindness better than 화기애애하다.

explain_en: Warm, friendly mood of a gathering or scene; describes atmosphere (분위기) It describes a gathering or atmosphere that is warm and pleasant, and it isn't used for a single person. '훈훈하다' stresses a feeling of warmth and kindness, while '화기애애하다' fits a mood where everyone is getting along, laughing and chatting.

t90.ax: The cheerful mood suddenly went quiet.

examples.en: A costume parade was held in the street during the festival.

examples.ko: 아이들이 동화 속 인물로 분장하고 가장행렬에 참가했어요.
examples.en: The children dressed up as fairy-tale characters and joined the costume parade.
People gathered along the road to watch the costume parade.
This year's costume parade was more colorful than ever.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 가장행렬에서 로봇 옷을 입기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our class decided to wear robot costumes in the parade.
After the costume parade ends, the fireworks begin.

explain: 사람들이 분장이나 변장을 하고 줄지어 걷는 행사예요. 그냥 줄지어 걷는 행사는 '행진'이나 '퍼레이드'라고 하고, 분장이 중요할 때 '가장행렬'이라고 해요. 축제나 학교 행사 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.example: 저도 올해 축제 가장행렬에 참가할 거예요.
phrases.en: I'm going to take part in this year's festival costume procession too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에 직접 나가 걷는 사람이 되었을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you personally join the procession as a participant.
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in a costume procession

phrases.en: A costume procession is held downtown on Halloween.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 있다는 사실을 알릴 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for saying that the event takes place.

phrases.en: I watched the parade on the last day of the festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분장이 꼭 없어도 쓸 수 있는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that doesn't require costumes.

explain_en: It is an event where people walk in a line wearing costumes or disguises. A plain march is called '행진' or '퍼레이드', and '가장행렬' is used when the costumes are the point. It comes up in talk about festivals and school events.

examples.ko: 관객들은 공연이 끝나자 큰 갈채를 보냈어요.
examples.en: The audience gave a big round of applause when the show ended.

examples.ko: 선수들은 팬들의 갈채 속에 경기장에 들어섰어요.
examples.en: The players entered the stadium amid the fans' cheers.
The clapping and cheering went on for a long time.
It was a wonderful performance that deserved acclaim.

examples.ko: 그는 갈채는 바라지 않고 묵묵히 일했어요.
examples.en: He worked quietly without wanting any praise.
His effort was rewarded with enthusiastic applause.

explain: '박수'는 손뼉 치는 행동이고, '갈채'는 소리 내어 크게 칭찬하는 뜻까지 담겨요. '갈채를 보내다/받다'로 쓰고, 말할 때는 보통 '박수'를 쓰며 '박수갈채'라는 짝말로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 공연에서 큰 갈채를 받았어요.
phrases.en: The singer received great applause at the concert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들에게 크게 칭찬받고 박수받는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being praised and applauded loudly by people.

phrases.en: Applause poured out when the show ended.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박수'와 '갈채'가 합쳐진 말로, 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compound of 박수 and 갈채, and the most common pairing.

phrases.en: The audience gave enthusiastic applause.
phrases.nuance_ko: '열렬한'을 붙여 박수가 아주 뜨거울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '열렬한' adds the feeling of very warm, passionate applause.

explain_en: '박수' is the act of clapping, while '갈채' also carries the sense of loud praise. It is used as '갈채를 보내다/받다', and in speech people usually just say '박수'. It also appears in the pair '박수갈채'.

t90.ax: He worked quietly without wanting any praise.

en: to open; to begin; to kick off

examples.en: The Olympics open next week.
The festival opened on Friday evening.

examples.ko: 프로야구가 개막하면 매주 경기장에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Once the pro baseball season starts, I'll go to the stadium every week.

examples.ko: 영화제가 개막하는 날 많은 배우가 왔어요.
examples.en: Many actors came on the day the film festival opened.

examples.ko: 공연이 개막해서 극장 앞이 사람들로 붐볐어요.
examples.en: The show opened, and the front of the theater was crowded with people.

examples.ko: 전시회가 개막할 때까지 준비할 게 많아요.
examples.en: There is a lot to prepare before the exhibition opens.

explain: 축제, 경기, 공연, 전시처럼 큰 행사가 시작될 때 써요. 반대말은 '폐막하다'예요. 수업이나 회의에는 '시작하다'를 쓰고 '개막하다'는 쓰지 않아요. '개막식', '개막 경기'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Many people came to the opening ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 시작될 때 하는 공식 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the official ceremony held when an event begins.

phrases.en: I went to see the opening game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 리그나 대회의 첫 경기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the first game of a league or tournament.

phrases.en: The show opens this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개막하다'와 같은 뜻이고 공연 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '개막하다', often used for performances.

explain_en: Festival, play, or sports season starts. Used when a big event such as a festival, sports season, show, or exhibition begins. The opposite is 폐막하다. For classes or meetings use 시작하다, not 개막하다. Nouns like 개막식 and 개막 경기 are common.

gh: formally open a meeting or session

p.n: Same meaning; the passive version sounds more impersonal.

examples.ko: 공중제비를 멋지게 돈 선수가 금메달을 땄어요.
examples.en: The athlete who did a great somersault won the gold medal.

examples.ko: 공중제비는 처음 배울 때 조금 무서워요.
examples.en: Somersaults in the air are a little scary when you first learn them.

examples.ko: 공중제비 한 번에 관중이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The audience clapped after one single somersault.
I tried doing a somersault at the swimming pool.
My older brother can even do a somersault.
I fell while doing a somersault and hurt my wrist.

explain: 몸을 공중에서 거꾸로 한 바퀴 돌리는 동작이에요. 보통 '공중제비를 돌다'처럼 '돌다'와 함께 써요. 바닥에서 구르는 '앞구르기'와는 달리 몸이 공중에 떠서 도는 동작이에요.

phrases.en: The athlete did a somersault and landed nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing.

phrases.en: It was amazing to see the child flip in the air.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌다'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 몸을 넘기는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '돌다', but with a sense of flipping over.

phrases.en: Today I practiced somersaults.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배우고 연습하는 이야기에서 명사 두 개를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Two nouns put together when talking about practicing.

explain_en: This is the move of flipping your body upside down once in the air. It is usually used with '돌다', as in '공중제비를 돌다'. Unlike '앞구르기' (a forward roll on the ground), the body is in the air while turning.

examples.en: The soldiers run around the field every dawn.

examples.ko: 방독면을 쓰고 구보하라는 명령이 가장 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The order to run while wearing a gas mask was the hardest.

examples.ko: 신병들이 아침마다 삼십 분씩 구보하면 체력이 좋아져요.
examples.en: If recruits run for thirty minutes every morning, their stamina improves.

examples.ko: 무거운 배낭을 메고 구보해서 어깨가 아파요.
examples.en: I ran carrying a heavy backpack, so my shoulders hurt.

examples.ko: 학생들이 선생님을 따라 줄을 맞춰 구보했어요.
examples.en: The students ran in line, following the teacher.

examples.ko: 어제는 비가 와서 실내에서 구보하지 못했어요.
examples.en: It rained yesterday, so we couldn't run indoors.

explain: '달리다'보다 훈련하듯 일정한 속도로 달리는 느낌이 있고, 군대나 훈련 이야기에서 주로 써요. 구령으로는 '구보!'처럼 짧게 말하기도 해요. 취미로 달릴 때는 '뛰다', '달리다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I can hear the soldiers running in the distance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun that follows.

phrases.en: Yesterday we ran in formation even though it rained.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체예요. 훈련을 했다는 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past polite form, used when talking about doing the drill.

phrases.en: I ran ten laps around the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구보하다'보다 쓰임이 넓고, 취미나 운동으로 뛸 때도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 구보하다, and natural for running as a hobby or exercise.

explain_en: Sino-Korean, formal verb for running at a steady pace, as in drills or exercise. Compared with '달리다', it feels like running at a steady pace as training, and it mostly appears in military or drill contexts. As a command it can be shouted short, as '구보!'. For running as a hobby, '뛰다' or '달리다' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: The soldiers run around the field every dawn.
